title: Godiva/Jezebel bare-critical-sphere k_eff V&V
description: Bare critical sphere k_eff for U-235 Godiva / U-233 Jezebel. Uses nu-bar(E) (MF=1/452) + fission spectrum chi(E->E') (MF=5) read straight off ENDF by njoy::nuclear_data::secondary, handed to openmc-libs::Nuclide. See crates/openmc-libs/docs/validation.md.

title: BROADR SIGMA1 + U-238 capture wing-pedestal fix
description: SIGMA1 free-gas kernel ported (rayon-parallel per point). Fixed the U-238 capture wing pedestal: root cause was RECONR grid coarseness (over-linearized wings), not SIGMA1 — added reconr::refine_resonance_grid (adaptive bisection to tolerance). RRR L1 vs OpenMC 0.30 -> 0.0007 at 900/1200 K.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-07-07 (RECONR grid density; SIGMA1 unchanged). RRR L1 0.30->0.0007.

title: RECONR: all 5 resolved-resonance formalisms parse + reconstruct (LRF=1/2/3/4/7)
description: SLBW/MLBW (LRF=1/2), Reich-Moore (LRF=3), Adler-Adler (LRF=4, via reconr::aa), R-matrix-limited (LRF=7, via crate::samm). SLBW/MLBW/RM verified (Godiva/Jezebel k-eff + U-238 Doppler). LRF=4/7 wired; verification tracked separately.
close_reason: Done and verified (SLBW/MLBW/RM); LRF=4/7 verification tracked in op-cjw.5 / op-cjw.2.

title: Port ERRORR (multigroup covariance, ~11.2k lines)
description: Next major NJOY module. Largest single file in the port so far. Also the real caller that enables SAMM's Want_Partial_Derivs / Want_Angular_Dist, so it unblocks the deferred SAMM derivative + angular routines.
notes: Active priority 2026-07-08: porting NJOY forward (ERRORR) is the current focus for the njoy crate.

title: Verify SAMM (LRF=7 R-matrix limited) end-to-end
description: All 6 SAMM phases translated for the RECONR-reachable (KRM=3/IFG=0, no derivatives/angular) core and wired into RECONR (reconr::add_rml_range). NOT run against a real LRF=7 evaluation (16O / 19F). Opus verification: reconstruct an LRF=7 nuclide and reproduce reference NJOY pointwise sigma(E).

title: SAMM mf2 eliminated-channel reorder index: gamma(igamma+1) vs derived igamma-1
description: In samm::mf2, the eliminated-capture-channel reorder reads gamma(igamma+1) (samm.f90:1186); three independent hand-derivations predicted igamma-1, with a worked example showing igamma+1 reads past the group's valid channel range. Ported literally + bounds-checked + flagged. Highest-priority thing to check against a real LRF=7 evaluation where the eliminated channel isn't first.

title: njoy-outram-park-fork — nuclear data (NJOY2016 Rust port)
description: All nuclear data: NJOY2016 ENDF port (RECONR/BROADR/THERMR/ACER/HEATR/GASPR/UNRESR/PURR/SAMM), Faddeeva, windowed-multipole, lean-ACE + WMP blobs, nu-bar/chi. Exposes the XsProvider surface other crates pull from. GPL-3.0.

description: CSG geometry, particle tracking, k-eigenvalue, Woodcock delta-tracking. Data-free: pulls cross sections from njoy-outram-park-fork. Godiva/Jezebel k-eff V&V. GPL-3.0.

title: CoolProp transport + VLE + ancillaries port
description: DONE 2026-07-08: ancillaries (p_sat/rhoL/rhoV, 131 fluids), Maxwell EOS VLE + T_sat + two-phase (p,h) quality, transport mu (20 fluids: collision_integral/powers_of_T dilute + Rainwater-Friend initial + modBH higher-order) and lambda (38 fluids: ratio_of_polynomials/eta0_and_poly dilute + polynomial/poly_and_exp residual). Critical enhancement + hardcoded-fluid transport (Water/CO2) deferred. Verified vs NIST (mu/lambda <1%) and literature VLE. Codegen extended (gen_fluid.py + regen_all.py emit _ANCILLARIES/_TRANSPORT consts + Fluid::ancillaries()/transport()).
notes: 2026-07-08: Helium hardcoded transport ported (Arp/McCarty/Friend viscosity + Hands/Arp conductivity; near-critical lambda_c omitted like the rest). Added HardcodedTransport enum path to FluidTransport; codegen emits it for Helium. He mu(300)=1.99e-5 (lit ~1.99e-5), lambda(300)=0.156 (lit ~0.152). Helium now fully complete: EOS+flashes+VLE+transport all validated. Viscosity 21, conductivity 40 fluids. Remaining hardcoded (Water/CO2) still deferred.

title: Wire vendored openfoam_algorithms in coolprop to the CoolProp EOS + rename to OPCP
description: openfoam_algorithms/ was copied verbatim from tampines-steam-tables into outram-park-fork-coolprop (uom-only, no openfoam-basic-lib dep). Follow-ups: (1) rename TampinesSteamArray -> OPCP-prefixed; (2) replace its placeholder rho=psi*p correct_thermo with the CoolProp EOS via OPCPFluidSingleCV / flash (state_ph per cell); (3) once wired, drop the module-level #![allow(dead_code)]/unused_imports on the vendored tree; (4) OPCPFluidSingleCV + flashes are single-phase only (no saturation/VLE) — two-phase needs a dome solver (see op-kbc.7).
notes: 2026-07-08: deleted the other vendored solvers (driftFluxFoam, simplefoam, chtMultiRegionTwoPhaseEulerFoam) at user request — only the EOS-wired rhoPimpleFoam solver + shared openfoam_source remain. Remaining: single-phase only (no VLE), no transport (mu/alphaEff) from EOS, and openfoam_source still has unused primitives (dead_code allow stays until rhoPimpleFoam exercises them).

title: Port more fluids beyond Water (run dev/gen_fluid.py)
description: Add fluids relevant to the FHR/multiphase work + common working fluids: run dev/gen_fluid.py <Fluid>, add a Fluid enum variant + fluids/mod.rs decl. The codegen already errors on unsupported term types (e.g. IdealGasHelmholtzCP0PolyT), flagging which fluids need new term-type support in the engine.
notes: 2026-07-08: ALL 137 CoolProp pure fluids now wired into the Fluid enum (was 9). Added dev/regen_all.py which runs gen_fluid.py over every fluid JSON and rewrites src/fluids/mod.rs + src/fluid.rs (enum, eos() dispatch, Fluid::ALL). Variant naming: CoolProp name, non-alnum removed, tokens capitalised (n-Heptane->NHeptane, R1234ze(E)->R1234zeE, digit-leading->F prefix). Added Fluid::ALL slice + tests/all_fluids_smoke.rs (every fluid finite/positive critical pressure within 25%). gen_fluid.py now emits #![allow(clippy::approx_constant)] (EOS coeffs near pi are data). Fluid data ~0.5MB total, clippy clean. Per-fluid reference tests beyond the 9 pinned are the remaining follow-up.

title: Density-solve flashes: (T,p), (p,h), (p,s) inputs
description: Only (T,rho) inputs so far (the EOS natural variables). Add a robust density solver (bracket+Newton on p(T,rho)) for (T,p), then (p,h)/(p,s), matching CoolProp's PropsSI input pairs. Handle multiple roots (liquid/vapor) + phase determination.
notes: 2026-07-08: single-phase (p,T)/(p,h)/(p,s) flashes done (src/flash.rs); two-phase (p,h)/(p,s) quality via Maxwell VLE (src/vle.rs) done. Wired into OPCPFluidSingleCV (two-phase-aware).

title: Implement non-analytic critical-region residual terms (+ delta=1 handling)
description: eos::ResidualTerm::NonAnalytic::accumulate is currently a no-op; data is carried. Implement the IAPWS-95/Span-Wagner non-analytic term alpha + first/second delta,tau derivatives with the delta=1 (critical density) limit guard. Needed for accuracy within ~1% of the critical point (Water, CO2). Verify at Water critical/reducing state (p=22.064 MPa, delta=tau=1) and near-critical points.

title: Hardcode fluid/EOS data as Rust code -- no runtime JSON/file reads
description: CoolProp reads fluid EOS coefficients + ancillary equations from JSON (bundled/compiled). This fork hardcodes that data as Rust constants/data structures (const arrays / typed structs), so there is NO runtime file or JSON parsing and the data is rust-analyzer-navigable. Likely a codegen step (script that reads CoolProp's JSON once at authoring time and emits Rust source) rather than hand-transcription -- decide codegen vs hand-port when starting. Mirrors njoy's embedded-data-blob approach.
close_reason: Hardcoded const fluid data via dev/gen_fluid.py codegen (JSON -> Rust, EOS-only data reduction); no runtime JSON. Water.rs = 3KB full IAPWS-95.

NOTE: rfluids may require the CoolProp native lib / build toolchain on the test host -- confirm its build requirements and licensing (CoolProp is MIT). Dev-dep only, so it does not affect the shipped crate.

title: Scope decision: which CoolProp backend + fluid subset to port first
description: CoolProp is large. Suggested first slice: the HEOS (Helmholtz-energy-explicit) backend for a handful of pure fluids -- start with Water (CoolProp's IAPWS-95, which cross-checks the user's tampines-steam-tables IAPWS-IF97), then common refrigerants / working fluids relevant to the FHR + multiphase work (e.g. the salts/coolants of interest). Defer incompressible backend, humid air (HAPropsSI), mixtures, and the tabulated TTSE/bicubic backends. User to confirm the target fluid list + backend order before starting.

title: Design: enum dispatch for backends/fluids (no trait objects)
description: Per workspace rule + user requirement: model CoolProp's AbstractState/backend polymorphism (HelmholtzEOSMixtureBackend, IncompressibleBackend, HumidAir, ...) and the fluid set as Rust ENUMS with match-based dispatch -- no Box<dyn Trait>/&dyn. Traits may still enforce a per-backend method contract at compile time, just not for runtime dispatch. Exhaustive matches make adding a fluid/backend a compile error until handled.
close_reason: Enum dispatch established: Fluid enum, ResidualTerm/IdealTerm enums, match-based term accumulation. No trait objects.

title: outram-park-fork-coolprop — CoolProp thermophysical properties (Rust translation)
description: New workspace crate: a pure-Rust translation of CoolProp (https://github.com/CoolProp/CoolProp, MIT, C++ thermophysical property library — Helmholtz-energy-explicit EOS backend for ~120 pure/pseudo-pure fluids + mixtures, plus incompressibles and humid air). Named with the outram-park-fork- prefix from the start (external-project fork, per the trademark-compliance convention op-ahi). Two hard design constraints from the user: (1) enum dispatch, NOT trait objects, for backend/fluid selection (matches the workspace no-trait-objects rule); (2) hardcode the fluid/EOS data as Rust code -- NO runtime JSON or other file reads (matches njoy's embedded-data philosophy + the workspace static-navigability goal). Verification uses the rfluids crate (https://github.com/portyanikhin/rfluids, a Rust interface to CoolProp) as a DEV-dependency oracle. Book-keeping only; not started.
notes:
Crate initiated 2026-07-08: outram-park-fork-coolprop (MIT, workspace member). CoolProp cloned into gitignored reference/. First vertical slice done + verified: Helmholtz engine (Power+Gaussian residual + Lead/LogTau/PlanckEinstein ideal, all derivs), (T,rho) property eval, Water (IAPWS-95) hardcoded (3KB via dev/gen_fluid.py codegen). Water pressure reproduces CoolProp triple-line 611.65 Pa to ~1e-4 at sat liquid+vapor (tests/water_reference.rs). Committed crate 64KB (reference/ 58MB gitignored).
Helium added 2026-07-08 -- verifies to machine precision at its critical point (no non-analytic term). Confirms the Power+Gaussian+ideal engine is exact; Water's ~1e-4 residual is purely the pending non-analytic term (op-kbc.6).

This full multiphase 'tampines' crate is distinct from tampines-steam-tables (the IAPWS-IF97 property library) and will compose teh-o-prke + tuas (once those drop their openfoam-basic-lib dep, op-e46.1 / op-4wl.1) plus nee_soon. title: Trademark-compliance crate renames: outram-park-fork-<project> prefix
description: Rename every crate that is a Rust translation/fork of an externally-trademarked open-source project to carry the outram-park-fork- prefix, so the name is unmistakably a fork and not the official project (see TRADEMARKS.md). Per-crate rename scope: (1) package name in the crate's Cargo.toml, (2) directory under crates/, (3) [workspace] members path in root Cargo.toml, (4) every path dependency on it in other crates' Cargo.toml, (5) every 'use <old_crate>::' / extern references in dependent crates + examples + tests, (6) publish metadata/README/docs mentions, (7) any CI / scripts referencing the path. crate:: self-references do NOT change (package-internal). Do the renames one crate at a time, leaning on the compiler as the reference checker (per CLAUDE.md). Book-keeping only for now — do not execute.
notes: New external-project forks (e.g. outram-park-fork-coolprop, op-kbc) are born with the outram-park-fork- prefix -- they need no rename, only the existing crates in this epic's children do.
